method: Bounded original-pixel study of the nine remaining kaf-vowel disclosures anchored to the same printed personal name. Only chapters containing annotations were inspected. Complete original glyphs/words and numbered rows verify exact locations. A same-page ordinary kaf foot demonstrates natural terminal bulk, while three local joined-point probes show saturated lower shapes; their existing canonical vowels are not used as proof. Genuinely detached same-font patah, tsere and qamats on mem/lamed establish the competing literal point contours without assuming a detached same-letter positive. None of the nine targets uniquely preserves one such contour. Native A2 pixels and integer nearest-neighbor crops only; no OCR, grammar, expected name spelling, translation, enhancement or blank-cavity inference. Algorithms replay image provenance and exact source conservation, not vowel readings. Prior reports remain immutable.

inspections.finding: The broad rounded lower mass ends in a small central projection, but that projection is inseparable from the natural thick kaf foot. No independent bar, pair or thin crossbar/stem survives to certify one vowel. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

The lower central projection is broadly fused to the foot. A filled pair, short stem or broadened bar can produce the remaining outline; the same-page joined probes do not discriminate them. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

The lower mass is squared off across a broad bottom. Its upper attachment is saturated and lacks the white separation or nodes needed to distinguish a short stem from merged dots or bar. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

A broad rectangular lower drop survives below the foot, but its shoulder and the natural terminal are coalesced. Its flat bottom alone cannot decide between the competing point classes. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

The rounded lower mass has a flattened bottom and small side spur. Those irregularities do not resolve a two-dot waist, three-node group or qamats stem, and ordinary foot bulk remains part of the shape. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

A rounded lower projection with a tiny central tip remains. The point head is wholly fused into the foot, so the tip cannot uniquely distinguish a short stem from merged points. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

The source preserves a low rectangular projection with flat bottom, broadly merged into the foot. No thin T stem, pair waist or separable shallow bar makes one class certain. Both literal source brackets are preserved in the corrected whole-word locator. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

A broad flattened lower drop and a tiny low edge spur survive, but the drop has no independent head or aligned multiple nodes. Same-page ordinary foot and competing detached class anchors do not recover a unique vowel. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.

The lower contour tapers into a broad rounded drop. It remains fully fused to the naturally heavy foot and does not preserve an independently classifiable bar, pair or stem. Retain the complete disclosure; no expected name spelling or grammatical vocalization supplies a mark.
